intro: The kitchen is the heart of every villa — and the room that suffers most in Bali's climate. Steam, splashes and tropical humidity destroy chipboard cabinets in months. We build kitchens on moisture-resistant marine plywood carcasses with sealed edges, stainless or aluminium plinths and quality soft-close hardware, so doors stay aligned and drawers keep gliding year after year.

Whether you want a minimalist handle-less kitchen, a warm solid-teak tropical kitchen, a Japandi look in oak-tone veneer or a high-gloss painted finish, we design around your layout, appliances and the way you cook. We also build butler's pantries, kitchen islands with seating, open-air outdoor kitchens and compact kitchenettes for rental villas.

Clean modern lines with J-profile, gola channels or push latches.

kitchens.materials: Carcasses in 18 mm marine-grade (WBP) plywood, sealed on all edges. Fronts in HPL, two-pack (duco) paint, teak veneer, or solid teak. Hardware from Blum, Hettich or Hafele-grade equivalents with soft-close. Plinths in aluminium or stainless steel to resist mopping water.

faqs.q: What is the best material for a kitchen in Bali?
faqs.a: For the cabinet boxes, marine-grade plywood is the most reliable choice in Bali's humidity — far more stable than MDF or particle board. For doors, HPL laminate is the most durable and easiest to clean, two-pack paint gives a seamless modern look, and solid teak gives the warmest tropical character.

faqs.q: Do you install countertops and appliances?
faqs.a: We supply and fit countertops in terrazzo, granite, quartz, marble or solid surface through trusted stone partners, and we can install built-in appliances, sinks and taps in coordination with your plumber and electrician.

faqs.q: How do you protect kitchens against termites?
faqs.a: All timber and plywood is treated with anti-termite preservative before assembly, cabinets sit on raised legs or sealed plinths, and we leave inspection access behind the plinth. We also recommend a professional soil treatment for new builds.

intro: A good wardrobe in Bali does more than store clothes — it protects them. In a closed cupboard, tropical humidity quickly turns into mould and musty smells. Our built-in wardrobes are designed to breathe: ventilated plinths and tops, rattan or louvred door options, moisture-resistant boards inside and space for a dehumidifier or a low-wattage warm light.

We build floor-to-ceiling fitted wardrobes for master bedrooms, guest rooms, kids' rooms and rental villas, with hanging space, drawers, shoe racks, safes and luggage storage planned around how you live. Choose from sliding doors, hinged doors, Balinese rattan panels, teak louvres, mirrored fronts or seamless painted finishes.

features.d: Smooth top-hung or bottom-rolling sliders, or hinged doors with soft-close.
Breathable natural fronts that look beautiful and prevent mould.
Vented plinths and tops, airflow gaps and optional dehumidifier space.
Double hanging, pull-out trouser racks, drawers, safes and LED lighting.

wardrobes.materials: Carcasses in 18 mm plywood (marine-grade in bathrooms and coastal villas), with HPL or melamine-faced interiors for easy cleaning. Doors in HPL, two-pack paint, teak veneer, solid teak frames with rattan, or mirror. Sliding systems and soft-close hinges rated for tropical use.

faqs.q: How do you stop mould inside wardrobes in Bali?
faqs.a: We design wardrobes to ventilate: vented plinths and tops, small gaps behind back panels so air can circulate off the wall, breathable rattan or louvred doors where suitable, and wipe-clean interiors. A small dehumidifier or a low-heat LED strip inside makes a big difference too.

faqs.q: Sliding or hinged doors — which is better?
faqs.a: Sliding doors save space in smaller bedrooms and suit modern designs. Hinged doors give full access to the whole wardrobe at once and are easier to fit with rattan or louvred panels. We'll recommend what suits your room after measuring.

faqs.q: Can you build wardrobes on uneven walls and floors?
faqs.a: Yes. Bali villas often have walls and floors that are out of level. We scribe and adjust every wardrobe on site so it fits tightly to the walls and ceiling with clean, even gaps.

intro: A walk-in wardrobe turns getting dressed into a daily pleasure. We design and build bespoke walk-in closets and dressing rooms for villas and family homes across Bali — from a compact walk-through between bedroom and ensuite to a boutique-style dressing room with a central island, display shelving and statement lighting.

In the tropics, a walk-in wardrobe has to be planned around air. Open shelving, glass-fronted cabinets and air-conditioned or dehumidified rooms keep clothes, shoes and bags in perfect condition. We plan the layout in 3D with you, then build every section in our workshop for a precise, fast installation.

features.d: See your walk-in closet in 3D before anything is built.
Central islands with drawers, jewellery trays and a stone or glass top.

faqs.q: How big does a room need to be for a walk-in wardrobe?
faqs.a: A single-sided walk-in works from about 1.5 m wide; a two-sided layout from about 2.1 m; and a U-shape or island layout from about 3 m × 3 m. We can also convert part of a large bedroom into a walk-in closet with a partition.

faqs.q: Should a walk-in wardrobe in Bali have air-conditioning?
faqs.a: We strongly recommend either air-conditioning, a dedicated dehumidifier or excellent cross-ventilation. Without it, humidity can damage leather, shoes and delicate fabrics. We can integrate vents and dehumidifier housings into the design.

faqs.q: Can you add lighting and power?
faqs.a: Yes. We integrate LED strips, motion sensors, mirror lights and sockets for steamers or chargers, coordinating with your electrician.

faqs.q: Will a wooden vanity survive in a Bali bathroom?

intro: Doors and windows have to fight Bali's weather every day — driving rain, intense sun, humidity and termites. We make them in kiln-dried solid teak, merbau or bengkirai, with proper joinery, so they stay straight and keep closing smoothly.

faqs.q: Why do wooden doors warp in Bali, and how do you prevent it?
faqs.a: Warping happens when wood isn't dried properly or is sealed on one side only. We use kiln-dried timber, stable engineered cores for large doors, and seal all six faces — including top and bottom edges — before installation.

faqs.q: Do you install doors and windows in existing villas?
faqs.a: Yes. We replace old doors and frames in existing buildings, including removal, adjusting openings and making good around the new frame.

faqs.q: Teak or merbau — which should I choose?
faqs.a: Teak is the most stable and naturally weather-resistant, with a beautiful golden tone. Merbau is very hard and durable with a darker reddish colour and is often more economical for large quantities.

intro: Decking is where villa life happens — around the pool, on the terrace and on the rooftop at sunset. In Bali, a deck needs to cope with sun, heavy rain, chlorinated water and termites. We install hardwood decking in merbau, ulin (ironwood) and bengkirai, and premium WPC composite for low-maintenance areas.

Correct installation matters as much as the timber: we build on treated or galvanised steel frames with proper spacing and drainage, use stainless steel fixings or hidden clips, and finish with UV-protective oil.

Outdoor living areas built on stable, ventilated frames.

decking.materials: Merbau, ulin (Borneo ironwood) or bengkirai hardwood; WPC composite boards; treated timber or galvanised steel substructures; stainless steel screws or hidden clip systems; UV-protective deck oil.

faqs.q: What is the best decking wood for Bali?
faqs.a: Ulin (Borneo ironwood) is the hardest and most durable but more expensive. Merbau and bengkirai offer an excellent balance of durability and price. For zero maintenance, composite (WPC) is a good option, though it can get hotter underfoot in full sun.

faqs.q: How often does a timber deck need oiling?
faqs.a: In Bali's sun we recommend re-oiling exposed decks every 6–12 months to keep the colour and protect the surface. Left unoiled, hardwood will weather naturally to a silver-grey.

faqs.q: Do you build the frame too?
faqs.a: Yes. We build the substructure in treated hardwood or galvanised steel with correct spacing and drainage — the most important part for a deck that lasts.

kitchen-cost.title: How Much Does a Custom Kitchen Cost in Bali? (2026 Guide)
kitchen-cost.meta: A practical 2026 guide to custom kitchen prices in Bali: cost per metre for HPL, painted and teak kitchens, countertops, hardware and what affects your quote.
kitchen-cost.h1: How much does a custom kitchen cost in Bali?
kitchen-cost.intro: Kitchen prices in Bali vary enormously — from cheap particle-board kitchen sets that fall apart in a year to luxury teak kitchens that last decades. This guide explains how kitchens are priced in Bali, what drives the cost and how to compare quotes properly.

sections.h: How kitchens are priced: per linear metre
p: Most Bali workshops price kitchens per linear metre (in Indonesian: per meter lari) — the length of the cabinet run measured along the wall. A price per metre usually includes the base cabinets and the wall cabinets above them. Tall units, islands, countertops, appliances and sinks are normally priced separately.
When comparing quotes, always check whether the price per metre includes wall units, interiors in the same finish, edge banding on all edges, hardware brand and installation.
Plywood carcass with HPL fronts: from around Rp 3.5–5 million per linear metre. This is the best-value, hard-wearing option for most villas and rentals.
Two-pack painted (duco) fronts: from around Rp 4.5–7 million per metre, for a seamless modern look in any colour.
Solid teak or teak veneer fronts: from around Rp 6–14 million per metre, depending on whether fronts are veneer or solid wood.
Kitchen islands start from about Rp 15 million; outdoor kitchens from about Rp 20 million. Stone tops typically add Rp 2.5–8 million per metre depending on the material.

sections.h: What drives the cost up (or down)
p: Carcass material: marine plywood costs more than particle board or MDF but is essential in Bali's humidity.
Finish: HPL is the most economical; painted, veneer and solid timber cost progressively more.
Hardware: soft-close hinges, full-extension runners, corner carousels and lift-up mechanisms from quality brands add cost but transform daily use.
Complexity: curved panels, integrated handles, glass fronts and lots of drawers take more workshop time.

sections.h: Where to save — and where not to
p: Save by choosing HPL for doors and fewer, wider drawers. Don't save on carcass material, edge sealing or hardware: these are what fail first in Bali.
Never accept particle board (chipboard) in a kitchen in Bali. It swells permanently the first time water gets in.

Send your floor plan or measurements, photos of the space, your appliance list and a few inspiration images. After a site visit we prepare drawings and an itemised quote with materials, hardware and timeline in writing.

materials.title: Best Wood & Materials for Furniture in Bali's Humidity
materials.meta: Teak, merbau, ulin, marine plywood, MDF or HPL? A practical guide to choosing furniture materials that survive Bali's humidity, salt air and termites.
materials.h1: The best wood and materials for furniture in Bali's climate
materials.intro: Bali's humidity, salt air and termites destroy the wrong materials quickly. Here is a straightforward guide to what works in the tropics — and what to avoid.

p: Teak (jati) is the gold standard: stable, naturally oily, resistant to water, rot and termites, and beautiful. Plantation teak is widely available in Bali; older recycled teak is prized for character.

Merbau is very hard and durable with a rich reddish-brown colour — excellent for doors, stairs and decking. Ulin (Borneo ironwood) is the toughest of all and ideal for decking, posts and shingles. Bengkirai is a durable, more economical choice for decking and outdoor structures.
Marine-grade (WBP) plywood is the best board for kitchens, vanities and wardrobes in Bali. Its cross-laminated layers and waterproof glue resist swelling and hold screws well.
MDF can be used for painted doors in dry, air-conditioned rooms, but it must be sealed on all faces. Particle board (chipboard) should be avoided: once it absorbs moisture it swells and crumbles.

HPL (high-pressure laminate) is tough, waterproof and wipe-clean — the most practical finish for kitchens and rentals. Two-pack (duco) paint gives a seamless look but needs careful application. Natural oils suit teak and outdoor timber; polyurethane gives a harder wearing surface indoors.

Choose stainless steel or quality coated hardware near the coast, and soft-close hinges and runners rated for humidity. Seal every edge and cut-out, raise cabinets off wet floors and build in ventilation for wardrobes.

Treat all timber and boards with anti-termite preservative before assembly, keep wood off direct contact with soil and concrete where possible, leave inspection access and arrange a professional soil barrier for new buildings.
